name: Easy Korean Stew (Yukgaejang) with NY Steak, Egg, Bok Choy & Radishes (Prep-Ahead)

instructions.primary_message: This recipe utilizes 4 medium food storage containers.
Wash and dry the fresh produce.
instructions.secondary_message:
6 baby bok choy
1 small bunch green onion (scallion)
1 bunch radish

instructions.primary_message: Quarter chili peppers lengthwise; seed and remove ribs with a spoon to reduce spice level. Mince and place in a medium bowl. (Be careful with chilis; do not touch your eyes and ensure you wash your hands after handling or wear gloves while preparing.)
Peel and mince garlic. Add to the bowl with the chili pepper, along with oil, soy sauce, and chili-garlic sauce, then whisk to combine the spice paste.
instructions.secondary_message:
4 clove garlic
toasted sesame oil
2 tbsp soy sauce
1 tbsp chili-garlic sauce

instructions.primary_message: Pat the steak dry with paper towels, thinly slice, and place in another medium bowl. Add half of the spice paste, stir to coat, and set aside to marinate. (Reserve remaining spice paste for the next step.)
instructions.secondary_message: 1 ½ lb striploin (New York strip) steak

instructions.primary_message: Using a clean cutting board, trim bok choy, then separate into leaves. Add to the bowl with the remaining spice paste.
Trim and cut green onions crosswise into 1-inch pieces. Add to the bowl.
Preheat a large pot over medium-high heat.
While the pot heats up, trim and quarter radishes lengthwise. Add to the bowl with the other veggies, stir to combine, and set aside.
Once the pot is hot, add oil and swirl to coat the bottom. Add steak and cook, stirring frequently, until starting to brown, about 2 minutes.

Add veggies and broth to the pot, then stir to combine the stew and bring to a boil. Once boiling, reduce to a simmer and cook, stirring occasionally, until steak is cooked through and veggies are tender, 2-3 minutes.
Meanwhile, place eggs and salt in a small bowl, then whisk to combine.
When the stew is done, slowly pour the egg mixture into the pot, while gently stirring, to separate into ribbons. Simmer until the egg is cooked through, 2-3 minutes. Remove from heat.
Divide stew between storage containers and set aside to cool completely, about 15 minutes. Cover and refrigerate until ready to eat. Heat stew in a saucepan or microwave and enjoy!
